in `/Users/ninawork/entire/entire-bundle-20260429-165951`, there are logs for a repo that had some issues migrating from v1 to v2. first, they got a bunch of failed checkpoints. then the user pulled in all the v1 branch changes, and then reran the migration command, only to see a bunch of them skipped.

then, the user deleted the v1 branch, but noted it came back at some point, which was unexpected to them (there is a possibility someone else was working with the repo that didn't have the v2 setting turned on - that's my guess).

then, the user discovered every time they pushed, messages like this:
```
gitsync on  main via :hamster: v1.26.2
❯ git push
[entire] Pushing v2/main to origin....
[entire] Syncing v2/main with remote.... done
[entire] Pushing v2/main to origin.... done
[entire] Note: .entire/settings.json sets checkpoints_version: 2. Run 'entire migrate --checkpoints v2' to migrate existing checkpoints to v2.
[entire] Use 'entire migrate --checkpoints v2 --force' to rewrite all checkpoints in v2.
[entire] Pushing v2/full/current to origin.... already up-to-date
[entire] Pushing v2/full/0000000000007 to origin....
[entire] Syncing v2/full/0000000000007 with remote..... done
[entire] Pushing v2/full/0000000000007 to origin.... done
Everything up-to-date
```

it was rotating all the way to 0000000000007 even though the repo doesn't get that much traffic. that is a bug.

I’ll dig through the bundle logs first to reconstruct the sequence, then I’ll trace the v2 push/migration code path in the CLI. The “rotating to 0000000000007” clue sounds like either stale ref discovery or an index allocator being triggered during push, so I’ll look for both.

The bundle confirms the rotation increments in lockstep with fresh v2 writes: generation 1 around 10:38, then 2 and 3 within a minute, then 4, 5, 6, 7 on later commits. I’m narrowing now on the code that archives `v2/full/current`, because that should not happen on every ordinary checkpoint.

The noisy push line is partly expected from `pushV2Refs`: it pushes `/main`, `/full/current`, and the latest archive. The real bug is earlier: normal post-commit condensation is calling generation rotation every time it appends a checkpoint, so there is always a brand-new latest archive to push.

That makes one generation per new checkpoint until the current generation is reset cleanly everywhere. I’m checking migration/update paths now so the fix lands in the right layer rather than just hiding the push symptom.

content.text: I’ve got the shape of the bug now. I’m doing one quick local sanity pass over the edited tree so I can close this out with the exact files and verification status, not stale memory.

The working tree has the six intended Go files modified; the other untracked files were already sitting outside this fix, so I left them alone. I’m grabbing a few line anchors now so the final note points at the actual changes cleanly.

Fixed the v2 rotation bug.

Root cause: the v2 repair/update path only looked in `v2/full/current`. If a checkpoint’s raw transcript had already rotated into `v2/full/000000000000N`, rerunning migration treated it as missing and copied it back into `current`. That polluted `current` with old checkpoints, so later ordinary commits crossed the generation threshold and kept rotating, which explains the push reaching `0000000000007`.

I changed:

- [v2_committed.go](/Users/ninawork/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/v2_committed.go:91): search `full/current` plus archived `full/*` refs for transcript artifacts.
- [v2_committed.go](/Users/ninawork/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/v2_committed.go:287): update the generation where the checkpoint already lives, instead of always rewriting into `current`.
- [migrate.go](/Users/ninawork/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/migrate.go:249): migration repair now recognizes archived full artifacts and skips unnecessary repair.
- [push_common.go](/Users/ninawork/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/push_common.go:169): the push migration hint now ignores malformed v1 checkpoint entries with no summary, so those failed v1 artifacts don’t keep the hint alive forever.

Added regression coverage in [v2_generation_test.go](/Users/ninawork/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/v2_generation_test.go:440), [migrate_test.go](/Users/ninawork/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/migrate_test.go:515), and [push_common_test.go](/Users/ninawork/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/push_common_test.go:1392).

Verification:
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint ./cmd/entire/cli` passed
- targeted strategy tests passed
- `git diff --check` passed

One note: the v1 branch “coming back” can still happen if another client without the v2 setting writes or pushes v1 refs. This patch prevents v2 repair from rehydrating archived v2 data into `current`; it does not stop an older or differently configured collaborator from recreating v1 remotely.
Please make detailed commit messages outlining what changed and why

I’ll turn the finished fix into commits with bodies that explain the failure mode and the reason for each change. I’m going to keep the existing unrelated untracked files out of the commits and run the required pre-commit check before writing them.

The branch is `fix-checkpoint-gen-post-migration`; I’m splitting this into two focused commits: one for the v2 full-generation repair behavior, and one for the noisy v1 migration hint. First up is the repo’s required `mise run check`, which may take a bit.
